_comment: Tombstones for `Round N's item K` debts that a later round DISCHARGED. Read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/state_claim_check.py as finding S006. Round 390 built it, from a class this program has now hit three times. S004 already resolves an item pointer to the item's TEXT; nothing asked whether the item was still OPEN, so a discharged debt could be re-asserted forever and every checker stayed green. The failure is not carelessness: a next-steps block is written by copying the previous one and editing what the round touched, and a retired item is normally handled by DELETING its line -- which leaves no record that it was retired rather than merely omitted. A later block that re-expands a round-keyed compression ('the rest of language(C)'s standing items are unchanged') then has no way to tell the two apart, and resurrects it. This file is the missing tombstone.
_rules: An entry is a CLAIM and is held to the same standard as any other in this program: `evidence` must name a file, commit or artifact that a reader can open, and `retired_by` must be the round that actually discharged it -- not the round that noticed. Register only what you verified this round. A citation is exempt from S006 when its own item text acknowledges the closure (`closed`, `retired`, `discharged`, ...), because saying 'round 383's item 5 is CLOSED and must not be carried again' is the CURE, not the disease.

A resurrection, not a never-noticed closure -- which is why a tombstone and not a re-read is the fix.
